issue.title: `onDownloadProgress` never emits `percent: 1` for empty response bodies

arms.better: tm found the right source quickly and made the narrow correct change, then recovered from several tool-call failures. The PR's `test/stream.ts` snapshot passed all 19 AVA tests and the empty-body browser regression passed in Chromium; Firefox and WebKit could not launch because their Playwright executables were absent. The overall test result is recorded as failed because all changed tests could not complete, and `pnpm test` was blocked by the local pnpm install/build-script policy. It spent extra context on repeated searches and retries. The user-facing commands/messages were confusing during recovery: `tm ticket new --json` serialized the ID as a JSON string (our runner expected an object), `tm init` then said only that the existing project conflicted, and agent tool errors recommended retries even when an artifact enum needed correction. It also recorded `npm test` as a completed command because its shell pipeline masked the lint exit code; a clearer verification result should distinguish command exit status from the displayed tail output.

OpenCode gave a clear final summary and correctly identified that the full npm test command stopped at an unrelated lint error. However, it globbed the parent trial directory, selected the sibling `tm` clone, and edited `tm/source/utils/body.ts` instead of the OpenCode clone. It then claimed the fix was present without checking the OpenCode worktree; after the PR test snapshots were restored, empty-body download and upload progress tests failed in `test/stream.ts`, and Chromium also failed the hidden empty-body browser regression. Firefox and WebKit were unavailable in both arms. It needed to establish and verify its actual working directory before exploring or editing, and confirm the result against the intended clone's diff and regression tests.
